capabilities.target: Third-party enrichment API lookup, billed per call
Sub-agent that investigates an account, can itself spawn researchers
CRM account record enrichment fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch export of CRM account rows (40,000 rows)

instructions.note: 'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent... Keep going until every row is complete' sets no limit on retries, spawn depth, spend, or runtime. Combined with cap.spawn_researcher's ability to spawn further researchers and the 3% of rows that can never complete, this instruction drives an effectively unbounded loop.

elements.name: Outbound call to third-party enrichment API
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Per-run / per-day spend cap on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model in infrastructure or at the API gateway; works the same regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Max retry count and sub-agent spawn depth/count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the orchestration runtime, not by model compliance; a stronger model cannot call more times than the runtime permits.

controls.name: Real-time spend / usage anomaly alert on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: A monitoring system outside the agent; detection does not depend on the model's behavior.

controls.name: Dedicated API key/quota for the enrichment agent
controls.decay_rationale: A credential and quota boundary enforced by the API provider, independent of model behavior.

findings.title: Unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning can exhaust the shared enrichment quota (spend loop, TC6)

forecast.watch_signal: Nightly batch size growing beyond ~40,000 rows, median retries/spawns per row rising, or the shared quota being resized or reassigned (which would mask growing consumption); no new controls currently exist to fail further.

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call; the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, whose tools stop working until the next month if the quota runs out.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch (~1,200 rows) have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing repeated retry/spawn activity every run.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.
'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent... Keep going until every row is complete' with no stated limit.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run and per-day spend cap / call quota dedicated to the enrichment agent that halts processing automatically when reached.
Add a maximum retry count per row and a maximum sub-agent spawn depth/count; route unresolved rows (e.g., malformed company names) to a human review queue instead of retrying indefinitely.
Add real-time spend and call-volume alerting on the enrichment API account so runaway consumption is caught before the shared quota is exhausted.
Give the enrichment agent its own dedicated API key and quota, separate from the shared sales/marketing key, so a runaway loop cannot deny service to other teams.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to enrich.lookup or the CRM, so spoofing of the agent's own identity cannot be assessed from prompt.md and runtime notes alone.
No information is given on whether prompt.md or the agent's tool configuration can be modified after deployment without review.
Runtime notes do not describe whether individual lookup, write, or spawn actions are logged with an identity attributable to the agent.

Sending account identifiers to enrich.lookup is the intended function of the agent; data_sensitivity is internal, not confidential or restricted, so this is not an unwanted disclosure beyond ordinary business use.
The agent's credential scope for enrich.lookup is fixed and shared; nothing in the design lets the agent grant itself broader access than it already has.
Artifacts do not state whether requests or responses to the enrichment API are integrity-protected in transit.
No detail is given on whether the connection to the enrichment API is encrypted or whether payloads are logged with sensitive contents.
Artifacts do not describe who can change the shared quota configuration or rotate the shared API key.
No information on how the shared API key is distributed to the agent and its sub-agents or whether it could leak through logs.
Artifacts do not describe how spawned researcher sub-agents authenticate or whether their identity can be distinguished from the parent agent.
No information on whether a spawned sub-agent's instructions or configuration can be altered mid-run.
Runtime notes do not state whether actions taken by a spawned sub-agent are logged separately from the parent agent's actions.
Spawned sub-agents investigate the same account using the same enrich.lookup capability as the parent; no broader data exposure beyond the parent's intended access is described.
Spawned sub-agents are described as inheriting the same enrich.lookup capability and shared credential as the parent, with no separate or broader grant described.
Artifacts do not state whether partially enriched or low-confidence results are written to CRM before a lookup is confirmed complete.
cap.crm_write only writes enrichment fields back into the existing internal CRM record for the same account; it does not expose data to a new audience.
Artifacts do not describe CRM write rate limits or whether 40,000 nightly enrichment writes could affect CRM availability.
Artifacts do not state how cap.enrich_lookup verifies the identity of the third-party enrichment API endpoint it calls.
No information on whether API responses from the vendor are logged with request identifiers to allow after-the-fact verification of what was returned.

rating.rationale: A single property finding drives this rating: the design has no spend cap, no retry/recursion limit, and no spend alert on a paid, shared-quota API, while prompt.md instructs the agent to retry or spawn sub-agents 'until every row is complete' with ~3% of every 40,000-row nightly batch guaranteed to never complete. Because the only source involved (the nightly CRM batch) is internal, not untrusted, and the harm comes from missing limits rather than a complete attacker-controlled path, this is scored under rubric section 5a (property findings), not the base attack-path matrix. The I-row/S3 base tier is 'high'; the A4 fully-autonomous, spawn-capable autonomy modifier would normally add a tier, but section 5a caps property findings at 'high' because no complete path to a worse outcome exists today. No credited controls exist (all four recommended controls are missing_recommended), so residual equals inherent, and no trigger pushes the forecast higher because there is nothing left to decay -- the fix is to add the missing structural controls, not to anticipate a future failure mode.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or runtime config was provided; credential scope for cap.crm_write, authentication to the enrichment API, and logging/audit behavior are inferred or unknown, which is why several STRIDE categories are marked not_assessed rather than scored.

Only a prompt and a short runtime-notes summary were reviewed; there is no way to verify from these artifacts alone that the limits described as absent (step, retry, spend) are in fact absent in the deployed system.
